critiques.issue: H4.1 says any code change re-draws the 3-seed mean with a paired sd of about 0.15 pp. On the Muon base, the last seven small changes moved the mean by +0.003, -0.06, -0.03, +0.05, +0.03, -0.02 and +0.007 pp. Five of them change the math: freezing the whitening bias, slicing to 30x30, BN recalibration, LS 0.1 and the Muon warmup. If sd were 0.15, the chance that all of them land within ±0.06 is roughly 0.3^7, about 2e-4. So the noise model is wrong for the current base. Either Muon trajectories are much less chaotic than SGD trajectories, or edits that leave the RNG stream unchanged give strongly correlated paired comparisons. Every 'within noise' verdict since E024 depends on this number.
critiques.suggestion: Before more one-factor sweeps, re-measure the paired noise on the tip. Make 2-3 math-neutral but numerically different edits (op reordering, fp32 vs bf16 NS accumulation), and separately one edit that shifts the RNG stream, such as an extra dummy randn in prepare. Split H4.1 into 'RNG-preserving' and 'RNG-shifting' noise. Then re-grade E024, E026, E033, E037 and E039 against the measured sd.

critiques.issue: Changing the base lookahead decay from 0.774 to 0.859 per sync should change the late average substantially. Yet the mean matched the previous tip to 0.003 pp (0.75463 vs 0.75460). That is the signature of a no-op. E034 already showed that this pipeline can silently drop a change under torch.compile (requires_grad freezing had no effect on the traced graph). A schedule constant captured at compile time, or an alpha schedule built elsewhere, would behave the same way. The tip description now claims lookahead 0.97^5, and H1.6 states 'averaging horizon is flat' as a finding, even though the tree itself says 'pending a no-op check'.

If they are identical, mark E028 as a no-op, strike the 'flat between 0.95^5 and 0.97^5' claim from H1.6, and re-run the averaging-horizon test (including sync every 3 steps).

critiques.target: Untried directions (augmentation, head/BN optimizer, data selection)
critiques.issue: No experiment has touched augmentation: removing translate (H1.8.2), brightness/contrast jitter (H1.8.1) and cutout are all untested, even though H1.8 is the natural complement to the finding that LS is flat. The 100x576 head was never moved to Muon or a normalized update, although E039 shows the head lr is sensitive in a regime where most knobs are flat. The BN-bias lr multiplier (x64) was never swept. H1.4 (selective backprop) has sat open since the start with no run and no retirement.
critiques.suggestion: Priority order after batch size: (1) head lr x1.5-2 (E039 suggests this direction), (2) remove translate-2 or add jitter, (3) BN-bias multiplier 32/128. Retire H1.4 explicitly if it will not be tried.

critiques.issue: Muon lr is flat from 0.16 to 0.24, then drops 1.04 pp on every seed at 0.36. A cliff this sharp, with no slope below it, is surprising, and the E019 post-mortem explanation (tail noise) was refuted by E025. Nobody has explained it, and lrs below 0.16 were never tested. One candidate: an early instability during warmup at the higher peak, interacting with the 1-epoch whitening-bias training or with BN. Another: overshooting given the per-step weight-norm projection.
critiques.suggestion: Before tuning further, log per-step train loss for lr 0.24 vs 0.36 on seed 1 in drafts/ to see where the gap opens. If the gap opens early, test lr 0.12 and a higher lr with a longer Muon warmup to map the plateau, since the plateau's position decides how robust the tip is.
